title: Book One · Chapter 110: The Damp Back Shelf
story:
The next afternoon, Mr Qiu's stall is closed across the front.

There is no large notice. Customers usually wait here. Now a board stands in that space. Mr Qiu is inside with Mr Han. The roof sheet hangs low over one corner.

Ronan stops beside Mum.

“Is he gone?”

“He is right there,” Mum says.

“I mean the stall.”

She looks at him, then at the board. “Let us ask Mr Qiu.”

Mr Qiu hears them and comes to the dry edge. His sleeve is wet. He is carrying six exercise books on a flat tray. Their back corners are dark and bent.

“The back shelf got wet last night,” he says. “I moved the good stock this morning. The roof needs work first. Then I can sell here again.”

“All the books?” Ronan asks.

“No. These six are damp. A little loose paper is worse. Most of the boxes stayed dry.”

Ronan looks through the gap. Rows of wrapped pencils and two piles of books are still dry. But he is afraid the stall may close forever.

Mr Han asks Mum to speak to Mrs Lan. They need to store two wooden crates somewhere dry. It is only for a short time. Mr Qiu will ask Mrs Lan first. She will decide about the crates.

“I can knock at her door,” Mum says. “The space is hers to decide about.”

Ronan reaches towards the exercise books.

“Careful,” Mr Qiu says. “The paper can tear when it is wet.”

He pulls his hand back. He was going to hold the books by their corners.

“Can I do something else?”

Mr Qiu looks round. “Tell the next customers the stall is closed today. Stay beside your mother. Do not stand in the road.”

Ronan wanted to work with the books. But Mr Qiu needs help with customers too. A woman comes to the stall at once. She has a little child with her. She asks for a pencil. Ronan gives her the message. She looks disappointed, then asks, “When will you open again?”

“I do not know yet,” Ronan says.

Mr Qiu comes over himself. He points to another stall. “You can buy pencils there.” Ronan looks surprised. Mr Qiu is helping her buy at another stall.

“She needs a pencil today,” Mr Qiu says after she leaves. “I cannot sell one safely from under that.”

He points at the heavy sheet. No one asks the children to lift it.

At home, Mrs Lan is not ready to say yes to the crates. How big are the crates? How long will they stay? Will wet things touch her floor? She asks all three questions.

Mum goes back to ask Mr Qiu. Ronan waits inside the green gate. He makes a small CLOSED TODAY card on dry paper. Mum returns with Mr Qiu's answer about the card. He has a board, but wants clearer letters.

“May I take this?”

“Tomorrow, with me. He must see it before we put it up.”

Ronan leaves it under a book to keep flat. He wants to write OPEN TOMORROW on the back. He stops with the pencil over the paper. No one promised that.

The rain grows softer after supper, but it does not end. Ronan listens for footsteps at the gate. He hopes Mr Qiu will come to speak to Mrs Lan. He wants to hear Mr Qiu's plan for the stall.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- damp＝受潮的
- stock＝存货
- crate＝木箱
- closed today＝今日暂停

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：tray＝托盘；tear＝撕破；notice＝告示。

## 读句提示

**When will you open again?**

你／什么时候／会重新营业？直接向Mr Qiu提问。

## 理解问题

1. MrQiu哪些东西湿了，哪些仍干燥？
2. MrsLan在决定借空间前提出了哪些问题？
